claims.text: Dose in HFrEF (start low, double every two weeks): metoprolol succinate 25 mg once daily (NYHA II) or 12.5 mg (more severe), up to 200 mg;
claims.quote: The recommended starting dose of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablet is 25 mg once daily for two weeks in patients with NYHA Class II heart failure and 12.5 mg once daily in patients with more severe heart failure. Double the dose every two weeks to the highest dosage level tolerated by the patient or up to 200 mg of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets.

claims.text: carvedilol 3.125 mg BID for 2 weeks, then 6.25, 12.5 and 25 mg BID, after fluid retention is minimized.
claims.quote: Prior to initiation of COREG, it is recommended that fluid retention be minimized. The recommended starting dose of COREG is 3.125 mg twice daily for 2 weeks. If tolerated, patients may have their dose increased to 6.25, 12.5, and 25 mg twice daily over successive intervals of at least 2 weeks.

claims.text: Interactions: digoxin, clonidine, diltiazem and verapamil add bradycardia (slowed AV conduction);
claims.quote: Digitalis glycosides, clonidine, diltiazem, and verapamil slow atrioventricular conduction and decrease heart rate. Concomitant use with beta blockers can increase the risk of bradycardia.

claims.text: stopping clonidine: withdraw the beta-blocker several days first (rebound HTN).
claims.quote: If clonidine and metoprolol are coadministered, withdraw the beta-blocker several days before the gradual withdrawal of clonidine because metoprolol may exacerbate the rebound hypertension that can follow the withdrawal of clonidine.

claims.text: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, quinidine) can double metoprolol levels.
claims.quote: Drugs that are strong inhibitors of CYP2D6 such as quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone were shown to double metoprolol concentrations.

claims.text: Higher epinephrine doses may be needed.
claims.quote: Higher doses of epinephrine might be necessary for patients taking metoprolol.

claims.text: Overdose: severe bradycardia, hypotension, AV block, bronchospasm and cardiogenic shock.
claims.quote: Overdosage of LOPRESSOR may lead to severe bradycardia, hypotension, and cardiogenic shock. Clinical presentation can also include AV block, heart failure, bronchospasm, hypoxia, impairment of consciousness/coma, nausea, and vomiting.

claims.text: Treat bradycardia with atropine, adrenergic drugs or pacing;
claims.quote: Bradycardia: Evaluate the need for atropine, adrenergic-stimulating drugs or pacemaker to treat bradycardia and conduction disorders.
Consider intravenous vasopressor infusion, such as dopamine or norepinephrine.

claims.text: shock with glucagon (bolus, then infusion if needed).
claims.quote: injection of glucagon (if necessary, followed by an intravenous infusion of glucagon)

claims.text: Hemodialysis is unlikely to help with metoprolol.
claims.quote: Hemodialysis is unlikely to make a useful contribution to metoprolol elimination
